title: Split OTLP ingest splitter for multi-backend routing with compatibility-mode shims
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: We currently funnel all OTLP span traffic through a single path that applies uniform sampling, tagging, and export semantics. This causes two operational issues: (1) high-cardinality or debug traces sent for investigation overload downstream Jaeger-compatible backends and increase storage costs; (2) some third-party backends (older Jaeger deployments, vendor Tempo instances) require minor schema tweaks (tag key renames, traceid format) and different retention signals.

Proposal: Implement a centralized OTLP ingest splitter service that performs two responsibilities: (A) split and route traces into parallel downstream pipelines based on policy (low-latency pipeline -> Tempo for production dashboards; buffered pipeline -> Jaeger-compatible stores for debug/forensics) and (B) apply lightweight compatibility-mode shims per-backend (attribute key rewriting, traceid normalization, and retention hinting). The splitter will operate as a horizontally sharded service sitting in front of exporter backends (managed by the trace-gateway layer). It will honor per-tenant routing rules and dynamic sampling overrides.

Design notes and trade-offs: 1) Centralized vs sidecar: centralization reduces code duplication and simplifies shims but requires careful autoscaling and tenancy isolation. We will implement multi-tenant sharding with token-based routing to avoid noisy-tenant interference. 2) Latency: the low-latency path will be synchronous and lightweight (no enrichment) to preserve dashboard SLOs. The buffered debug path will be asynchronous, using a persistent write-ahead queue with backpressure and TTL-based retention. 3) Schema changes: shims will be a small rule engine (YAML-driven) to rewrite attribute names and convert traceid formats; avoid heavy processing (no full-span reserialization) to keep CPU costs low. 4) Backfill/compat-mode toggles: operators can flip compatibility-modes per-backend to enable safe rollout for older vendors.

Operational concerns: autoscale policies, circuit breakers to avoid cascading failures, tracing of the tracing path (meta-spans), and observability for the splitter itself (ingest rates, drop/mutate counters). We will add SLOs for 95th percentile added latency per path and integrate alerts with PagerDuty.
acceptance_criteria: Splitter deployed behind trace-gateway and serving traffic in test environment with tenant sharding enabled
Low-latency path adds <5ms median latency and <50ms p95 overhead relative to baseline in canary tests
Buffered debug path persists to durable queue and delivers to Jaeger-compatible backend with <=60s delivery under normal load
Compatibility-mode rules can be toggled per-backend without restart and are applied to at least two rule types (attribute rename, traceid normalization)
Integration tests validate that per-tenant routing sends production spans to Tempo and debug spans to Jaeger test cluster
Metrics and dashboards created: ingest-rate, routed-bytes, dropped-spans, shim-transforms, per-backend latency breakdown
